A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GCA/DRT research despite the changed title and presentation. All 19 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling, training-efficiency, inference-cost, extrapolation, and MiniPile retrieval results in Tables 1–3 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 reports original language-modeling and efficiency results, plus summarization and RULER evaluations, in Tables 1–3 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The main GCA/DRT architecture remains, but v2 removes the standalone encoder-decoder variant, its auxiliary MLM schedule, and its external-corpus retrieval/re-encoding procedure. Equation 3 also changes the stated cross-attention normalization from standard softmax to softmax-off-by-one. These substantially narrow method scope while refining the retained mechanism.

E1.justification: PG19 and arXiv-math remain. v2 removes MiniPile training and corpus-retrieval evaluation, while adding XSum and CNN/DailyMail summarization and RULER single-needle retrieval and variable-tracking tasks. These introduce substantially different data and task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds YaRN-base (7B) and CEPE (7B) as reference comparators for single NIAH. The principal language-modeling comparator set remains Base LM, RPTContriever, Landmark Attention, and Block-Recurrent Transformer. Appendix E elaborates the existing Contriever-based RPT implementation rather than introducing another RPT baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds 350M configurations, including a 24-layer architecture, and downstream fine-tuning/evaluation with summarization scores and RULER accuracy, extending tests to 16M-token retrieval and 4M-token variable tracking. The language-modeling training budget remains unchanged. Table 1 also changes the 2K '+2 layers' baseline window from 658 to 704, although the prose retains 658; this is a conflicting reported setting, not evidence of rerunning.

E4.justification: v2 removes encoder and MLM ablations, restricts the Gumbel ablation to 16K evaluation, and adds Contriever and random-retriever controls on PG19/arXiv-math. Variable tracking provides a new diagnostic comparison of one versus two retrieval stages. The corpus-versus-self-retrieval study and arXiv-math extrapolation panel disappear. Figures 4–7 retain the earlier case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Both present point estimates; v2's additional result rows do not change this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises existing scores: Landmark Attention's 2K PG19 validation perplexity changes from 14.32 to 14.41, and DRT retrieval×2's 16K PG19/arXiv-math test values change from 13.32/2.91 to 13.18/2.85. The DRT revisions accompany method changes, so they do not establish an isolated same-setting gain. v2 adds 350M and downstream results, including 100% single-NIAH accuracy at 16M, while removing MiniPile results and 4K inference-cost rows.

T1.justification: Equation 3 substantively changes the mathematical cross-attention definition through softmax-off-by-one normalization. The chunk definitions, relevance-weighting equations, and training/memory complexity expressions remain. No new theorem or proof is introduced, and both Flash-GCA algorithms are unchanged.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes end-to-end causal retrieval, lower perplexity, and efficient training/inference. v2 makes 1000-fold length generalization with a fixed attention window and near-perfect 16M-token passkey retrieval central contributions, including a claimed field first. Its introduction also narrows the case-study claim from emergent long-range reasoning to evidence of causal retrieval.

C2.justification: v2 adds a hypothesis that chunk-level prediction supplies richer retrieval supervision than Landmark Attention's token-level objective, extending v1's explanation based on training-context length. Appendix E explicitly acknowledges that original RPT has stronger causal retrieval than the implemented Contriever substitute. Conversely, v1's corpus-retrieval failure discussion and its negative-sampling limitation are removed.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds the 350M architecture specifications, and Appendix E specifies RPTContriever's 64-token chunking and cosine-similarity retrieval. MiniPile training/indexing details, explicit per-model decoder/encoder parameter counts, and v1's code-release promise disappear. Shared optimizer, tokenizer, hardware, and Flash-GCA pseudocode remain; downstream fine-tuning details are sparse.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially redirects positioning toward attention and length generalization, adding positional interpolation, YaRN, attention sinks, LongAlign, Gemini 1.5, and Qwen2.5. The earlier dedicated discussions of efficient language modeling, retrieval-augmented models, and unsupervised dense retrieval are removed or substantially reduced, along with references such as REALM, Reformer, MiniPile, and Faiss.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, related work, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around length generalization. Training and inference sections merge, terminology changes from multi-hop to multiple retrievals, and the appendices are reorganized into A–E. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: The main text switches from one column to two columns. Table 1 gains parallel model-scale columns, and a new downstream-results Table 2 is introduced. The earlier efficiency table becomes Table 3 with fewer rows. Figure 3 drops its arXiv-math panel; architecture diagrams and case-study figures are retained but resized or relocated, with appendix cases spread across two pages.

improvement.justification: The summarization/RULER evaluations and retriever controls provide more direct evidence of useful long-context behavior than v1's perplexity and cases alone, while Appendix E improves transparency about RPT. The net gain is limited: downstream fine-tuning is underspecified, retained PG19 curves and pseudocode are not reconciled with revised table values and normalization, and the unsuccessful MiniPile corpus-retrieval study is removed rather than resolved.
